body: applies to the issuance of discretionary permits, approvals, licenses, and similar authorizations by the Department of Environmental Conservation related to the construction or expansion of data centers 50 megawatts or more in size but does not generally apply to approvals “deemed complete” by DEC before July 14th.  Moreover, it does not apply to approvals at the local level.

EO 62 imposes the moratorium until the Department of Public Service (“DPS”) submits a Generic Environmental Impact Statement and associated findings.  This submission will include a formal public comment and hearing process, and it will “assess the potential environmental impacts of the construction and operation of data centers in the State, including energy demand, water use and quality, air quality, disproportionate impacts on disadvantaged communities, and noise levels.”  This will be folded into an existing proceeding before DPS related to the creation of new rates and interconnection rules for data centers to ensure that these facilities do not worsen affordability concerns for New Yorkers.  The Governor has called this effort the “Energize New York” initiative.
